title: India becomes world's second-largest supplier of seafarers, overtakes China: Report
content:
• India has become the world's second-largest supplier of seafarers, contributing 311,936 seafarers, accounting for 12.16% of the global maritime workforce, according to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026.
• In 2015, India accounted for just 5.2% of the global seafaring workforce and ranked fifth worldwide, demonstrating a significant rise to its current second position.
• The Indian government is pursuing "Mission 20%", an initiative aimed at increasing India's share of the global seafaring workforce from 12.16% to 20% by the end of the decade.

title: Trump asks US Supreme Court to overturn $83.3 million E Jean Carroll defamation verdict
content:
• Donald Trump has asked the US Supreme Court to overturn an $83.3 million defamation judgment awarded to writer E Jean Carroll.
• Trump's appeal argues he is immune from civil liability for statements made while serving as president, relying on a 2024 Supreme Court ruling that granted presidents broad immunity for official acts.
• E Jean Carroll has already collected nearly $5.63 million from Donald Trump following a separate $5 million civil verdict for sexual abuse and defamation, after the Supreme Court declined to hear his appeal in that case.

title: Iran proposes temporary Strait of Hormuz deal with Oman, warns waterway will remain shut if rejected
content:
• Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi proposed a temporary traffic management system for the Strait of Hormuz, dictating specific routes through Iranian territorial waters for ships and limiting Oman's role to managing only part of the opposite lane.
• On July 20, Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement announced a blockade of Saudi ports on the Red Sea and subsequently claimed responsibility for launching ballistic missiles at a Saudi oil tanker.
• The Strait of Hormuz is a critical maritime route, through which roughly 20% of global oil exports and a significant share of liquefied natural gas (LNG) passed before the conflict.

title: Trump, Zelensky hold White House talks on Ukraine peace process, Patriot missile co-production
content:
• US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met at the White House on Tuesday, July 28, to discuss peace negotiations and co-production of Patriot missile interceptors.
• The Trump administration indicated it does not expect to spend the remaining $400 million in congressionally approved military aid for Ukraine until fiscal year 2029.
• Ukraine aims to manufacture Patriot missile interceptors under license domestically, a pledge US President Trump made during this month's NATO summit.

title: Trump privately questioned if Lindsey Graham's demanding travel schedule contributed to his death: Report
content:
• Senator Lindsey Graham died on July 11 at the age of 71, with preliminary findings indicating an aortic tear as the likely cause of death.
• US President Donald Trump is scheduled to deliver a eulogy at Senator Graham's funeral service at the Washington National Cathedral.
• Before his sudden death, Senator Graham had recently returned from a NATO summit in Türkiye and a visit to Ukraine.

title: Govt companies request RBI to extend concessional forex swap by three months
content:
• RBI introduced a US Dollar–Rupee Forex Swap Facility last month to provide currency hedging support to public sector entities for raising External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) of average maturity of three years or longer, with drawdowns between June 8, 2026, and December 31, 2026.
• Under the RBI special swap scheme, banks have mobilized over $20.7 billion in foreign exchange inflows till Friday last week.
• The US Dollar–Rupee Forex Swap Facility is undertaken in multiples of $1 million at a fixed rate of 1.5% per annum (compounded semi-annually).

title: Barclays sees RBI holding rates in Aug policy as FCNR(B) inflows ease rupee concerns
content:
• Banks have mobilised nearly USD 32 billion, primarily through FCNR(B) deposits, following the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) measures to attract overseas capital last month.
• Government securities have attracted more than USD 7 billion in foreign inflows since the RBI announced measures to attract overseas capital last month.
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to keep the benchmark interest rate unchanged at its August monetary policy review.

title: Macroeconomic fundamentals of Indian economy remain strong amid global challenges
content:
• Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) posted their highest-ever consolidated net profit of Rs 10,177 crore in 2025-26.
• Public Sector Banks (PSBs) achieved their highest-ever net profit of Rs 1.98 lakh crore and recorded a historic low Gross Non-Performing Assets (GNPA) of 1.9 per cent in 2025-26.
• The Government introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS 5.0) in May 2026, providing 100% guarantee coverage for MSMEs and 90% for non-MSMEs/airline sector, with a total credit flow of up to Rs 2,55,000 crore.

title: PSUs seek extension of RBI’s concessional ECB swap window
content:
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) withdrew the interest rate ceiling on fresh FCNR(B) deposits of 3-5 years’ maturity for NRIs, OCIs, and PIOs, with this special window open till September 30.
• The RBI launched a special US Dollar-Rupee forex swap window in June for Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) raising External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs), which is available till December 31, 2026.
• FCNR(B) deposits may have already surpassed the 2013 collection level of USD 26 billion in just 45 days, whereas in 2013, USD 26 billion was collected over three months.
